$comment: Studio section of the cross-platform backup zip. Recomputed by scripts/lib/studio-backup-reference.mjs in scripts/studio-contracts-check.mjs. Local rows use epoch-millisecond times (iOS / Android storage form; Web converts with toISOString). iOS has one database per account: seed rows whose accountPartition is not seed.partition, and assets only they reference, are not inserted there; iOS drops those ids from the expected lists too (expected assetIds include 4D…0006, referenced only by uid-b). Expected updatedAt is epoch milliseconds (Web compares Date.parse of its ISO value). Placeholders: $seed / $empty = the local states below; $export = exportCase.expect.studio or .entries; $exportLower = the same studio with every id except assetId lowercased; $exportWithoutA2 = export entries minus the original entry of asset 4D…0002. input.versionPatch (optional) overrides keys of studio.versions[0] after the placeholder is resolved; the value "$absent" deletes the key.

rules: data.studio is written only when the current partition has at least one non-deleted work; then BackupFile.version = 2, otherwise the file is byte-for-byte the version-1 format.

Readers accept version <= 2; above that the whole import is rejected (version_too_new). A file without data.studio leaves local works, rounds, versions, refs and their assets untouched in every import mode.

Exported scope: non-deleted works of the current partition; their rounds whose status is in exportedRoundStatuses; versions and roundRefs of those rounds; assets = distinct assetId of those versions and refs whose original bytes exist locally.

Row shape: exactly spec.fields per table, every field present (writers write null when absent). Readers treat a missing key as null and handle null as nullOnImport states: identifier, enum and flag fields, and any table that is null or missing, reject the whole import (unrecognized_format) at parse time, before any write; versions.width / versions.height must also be a JSON number equal to an integer in 1...2147483647 (0 or negative, fractional, a numeric string or out of range rejects the same way); the other non-null fields get the same default on every platform whether or not the local column is nullable, and the remaining nullable fields keep null; every non-null value must match typeOnImport.fields (type, range, enum set, shape, unique keys), else the whole import is rejected the same way; UUID-shaped work / round / version / chat ids uppercase, other strings verbatim, assetId verbatim (image-store key, case-sensitive; asset 4d…0001 is lowercase); times ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds; presetIds / params / modelRef / adjustments as JSON values, not strings; arrays sorted by primary key ascending in UTF-16 code-unit order, case-sensitive (roundRefs by roundId then order).

asset.mime = mime of the lowest-id version using that asset, else the sniffed mime of the original bytes, else application/octet-stream (never null). Entries: original studio-assets/<assetId>, thumbnail studio-assets/<assetId>.thumb (assetId verbatim) (only when stored locally); both recorded in attachmentChecksums under the full entry name.

Import, importNew and merge: a backup work whose id already exists in the current partition (tombstone included) is skipped with all its rounds, versions, refs and assets. Otherwise the work and its rounds / versions / refs are written with accountPartition = current partition, baseRevision = 0, syncState = pending, other fields as in the backup.

Import, replaceAll with data.studio: all works of the current partition (tombstones included) and their child rows are deleted first, then every backup work is written as above. Asset ids of deleted rows are handed to the orphan sweeper purge after commit (it rechecks every studio and chat reference); never delete them directly.

Assets: an asset already stored locally is kept as is. Otherwise its original is written when the entry exists, and its thumbnail when the .thumb entry exists, else ensureThumbnail runs after the rows commit. A missing original leaves the rows written.
All studio rows of one import are committed in one database transaction; assets written by this import are deleted again if that transaction fails.

Any import mode (v1 or v2) must not remove assets still referenced by studio rows: image cleanup after a conversation replaceAll goes through the orphan sweeper purge, not a direct delete or a whole-directory swap.

importCases.note: Backup without studio section: local works, rounds and assets untouched in every mode, replaceAll included.
Fresh device restore; A4 has no thumbnail entry so it is regenerated.
Same work id already in this partition (tombstone included): whole work skipped, local row kept.
Partition works replaced; old assets go to the orphan sweeper, which keeps A1 (new W1) and A9 (chat) and purges A10; other partition untouched.
Work / round / version ids read case-insensitively and stored uppercase; assetId (and entry names) kept verbatim.
Original entry missing: rows still written, asset not written, no thumbnail work for it.

The file version gate runs before the size check: a too-new file reports version_too_new even with a bad size.
Sizes are judged by numeric value: 1024.0 equals an integer in range and is accepted (JSON does not distinguish integer and fraction literals).

nullOnImport.$comment: Reader handling of null / missing fields in data.studio. Every case starts from input; patch maps a table to: an object = set those keys on the first row of that table in the exported section ("$absent" deletes the key), null = the whole table is null, "$absent" = the table key is removed. expect.error: the import is rejected (unrecognized_format) before any write. expect.reexport: the import succeeds; exporting again, the row with the same primary key as the patched first row (roundRefs: roundId + order) has these field values (times as exported ISO strings).

typeOnImport.$comment: Reader type / shape table for data.studio. fields: every field of every table with its type and onNull (null or a missing key; reject / default / keep, as nullOnImport). Types: uuid = RFC 4122 form (8-4-4-4-12 hex, version 1-5, variant 8/9/a/b, any case; primary keys works.id / rounds.id / versions.id); id = non-empty JSON string; string = any JSON string, verbatim; bool = JSON true / false only; int = JSON number equal to an integer in [min, max] (3.0 accepted, numeric strings rejected); number = finite JSON number >= 0; time = exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ that formats back to the identical string, between 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z and 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z; enum = one of enums[enum] (an unknown value rejects; a writer adding a value must bump fileVersion); idList = array of id; presetIds = object, style a string / null / missing, effects an array of strings / null / missing, stored verbatim; object / array = any JSON object / array, stored verbatim. Shape: data.studio an object, the five tables arrays, every row an object; unknown keys in a row or in data.studio are ignored (not stored, not exported). uniqueKeys: duplicate keys in a table (UUID-shaped ids compared upper-cased, other ids and assetId verbatim; ints compared as numbers, so -0.0 equals 0) reject. UUID-shaped = RFC 4122 form, version 1-5, variant 8/9/a/b. Numbers are read as IEEE-754 doubles first (1.0000000000000001 is the integer 1; exponent forms like 2e0 accepted). Duplicate member names in one object: the last one wins (validate and decode the same parsed tree). Any violation rejects the whole import (unrecognized_format) at parse time before any write, after the version_too_new check. Integrity cases lock the current behaviour: rows whose round / work is not in the backup are not written, versions take their round's work id, an asset missing from assets leaves the rows written without the image, dangling ids are stored verbatim. Cases start from input; ops apply in order to the exported section: {set: path, value} sets the value at path (path [] = data.studio itself; [table] = the table; [table, n] = row n; [table, n, field] = a field; value "$absent" deletes the key); {append: table, copyOfRow: n, set: {field: value}} appends a copy of row n with those fields overridden. expect.error / expect.reexport as nullOnImport (expect.reexportKey {table: {primary key fields}} looks up that row instead of the unpatched first row; "$absent" = no row with the primary key of the unpatched first row; a field "$absent" = the key is not exported). JSON.parse cannot keep 3 and 3.0 apart, so integral floats (accepted for every int field) are tested natively per platform (import_integerFieldsIntegralFloat_accepted).

fileShell.$comment: Raw bytes of the backup zip entry data.json. Each case gives the entry bytes as text (UTF-8 encoded) or base64. Consumers build a backup zip holding only data.json with these bytes, read it through their production backup-file parser, then import mode importNew into an empty local state. expect.workIds = the imported work ids; expect.error = the whole import is rejected (unrecognized_format, or version_too_new from the version check) before any write. Rules: strict UTF-8 only (a leading UTF-8 BOM is skipped; malformed bytes, encoded surrogates, UTF-16 reject); strict JSON (surrounding whitespace allowed; trailing content, unquoted names or values, single quotes, NaN reject); duplicate member names, version / data / studio included, the last one wins, names compared after unescaping; a number that reads as a non-finite double, or an unpaired surrogate escape, anywhere in the text (values later overwritten by a duplicate name included) rejects; version is a JSON number equal to an integer (2.0 accepted; above the readable maximum = version_too_new at any magnitude) and data an object; header keys createdAt / appVersion / platform / checksum (strings), containsKeys (boolean), data.providers / data.conversations (arrays) are required; nesting depth (root = 1) at most 128; checks run file-level JSON validity, then the version gate (above the readable maximum = version_too_new), then the shell shape; number literals of any length read as doubles. Consumers run every case twice: inside the zip (exact expect) and as a plain .json backup file (expect.error = rejected with no write, any error code).

cases.note: Minimal backup: header keys, empty providers / conversations, one work with one round.
A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped (RFC 8259 section 8.1).
Bytes are decoded as strict UTF-8; a malformed byte is not replaced with U+FFFD.
Only UTF-8 is read (RFC 8259 section 8.1).
data.studio appears twice: the last one is read.
Member names compare after JSON unescaping.
A number that reads as a non-finite double anywhere in the file rejects.
An unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escape in any string or member name rejects (RFC 8259 section 8.2).
Strict JSON only: no lenient extensions.
The scan covers the whole text, values later overwritten by a duplicate name included.
version is a JSON number equal to an integer; data is an object.
Any integral version above the readable maximum is version_too_new, whatever its magnitude.
An integral version below every integer range has no lower bound and imports normally.

Check order: file-level JSON validity, then the version gate, then the shell shape; a version above the readable maximum reports version_too_new even when the header or data no longer match this shape.
File-level JSON validity is checked before the version gate.
version has no lower bound beyond being integral.
Nesting depth = open objects and arrays at the deepest point, the root object counted as 1; at most 128.
Number literals of any length are read as doubles; only a non-finite result rejects.
Header keys createdAt, appVersion, platform, checksum (strings), containsKeys (boolean) and data.providers, data.conversations (arrays) are required with these types.
Header encryptedKeys is optional: absent or null, otherwise a string; any other JSON type rejects the file (shell shape, after the version gate).
